stem: A 66-year-old woman who travels seasonally for farm work presented on her own three months ago with cough and weight loss and was diagnosed with MDR-TB after testing; she was started on an appropriate second-line regimen. She was not identified through any organized screening or contact-tracing program. She has significant, longstanding heart failure. At today's follow-up, she reports increasing breathlessness, and vitals show oxygen saturation 90% on room air, respiratory rate 27/min. Exam: thin, bilateral crackles, mild peripheral edema consistent with known heart failure.

patient.social_history: Travels seasonally for farm work; presented for care on her own, not via any screening program
patient.presenting_complaint: Follow-up during treatment for MDR-TB: increasing breathlessness, new hypoxia and tachypnea today
patient.exam_findings: SpO2 90% room air, respiratory rate 27/min, thin, bilateral crackles, mild peripheral edema consistent with known heart failure
patient.prior_treatment: 3 months of second-line anti-TB therapy to date; no prior TB treatment before this episode

distractors: Her known heart failure proposed as sufficient explanation for the breathlessness and low oxygen saturation without considering a change from her documented baseline
Her demanding travel schedule proposed as a practical reason any change in management would be difficult to implement
ntep_correct_actions: Escalate or refer this patient to a higher-tier facility now, since her oxygen saturation (90%) and respiratory rate (27/min) each independently meet the quantified red-flag criteria that mandate referral.

Recognize that even though this patient presented on her own rather than through an active case-finding drive, NTEP's policy is to run active case-finding as standing, unconditional program activity across defined risk groups.
who_correct_actions: Base the decision to refer or escalate her care on individualized clinical judgment of her hypoxia and tachypnea; there is no WHO-specified quantified threshold mandating escalation, only a general direction toward decentralized care where it is safe.

Recognize that this patient's passive, self-initiated presentation is consistent with WHO's own conditional approach: general-population active case-finding is only recommended where local TB prevalence has been shown to meet a specific threshold (approximately 0.5% or higher).
us_correct_actions: Base the decision to hospitalize or refer this patient on individualized clinical judgment regarding her hypoxia and tachypnea, since there is no codified, quantified, nationally standardized threshold-based triage protocol in this framework either.

Attribute her case identification to her own symptomatic presentation, consistent with this framework's passive, contact-investigation-driven case-finding model rather than population-level active case-finding.
critical_error_conditions: Attributing the drop in oxygen saturation entirely to her known heart failure and taking no action in response to today's vitals
expected_divergence_points: Whether her current vital-sign abnormalities trigger a mandatory, quantified escalation/referral or are left to individualized clinical judgment
Whether active case-finding is standing, unconditional national program policy or conditional on a demonstrated local prevalence threshold
